paragraphs.heading: A conference I did not expect
paragraphs.edited: Not too long ago I went to a national conference that was a part of a movement designed to change the church's view of same-sex relationships. I went there not to rain on anybody's party, but to understand what this movement was about, and just to meet people personally, kind of from the inside. Well, it was like any other conference that I'd been to. There was worship, there were testimonies, but there were also 90-minute sessions where the leaders went into depth on some of the biblical passages, arguing that the church has been wrong about same-sex relationships for 2,000 years. But when they were done, the head person got up there and said, we've assigned each of you at this conference to go to a small classroom, and now you're going to role-play the talking points that you've learned, so you can go back and have conversations with people when you get back home.

paragraphs.heading: A time when I blew it
paragraphs.edited: In contrast to this first story, let me tell you about a time when I blew it. My senior year in college I took a class on apologetics. I was ready and anxious to have a conversation with anybody who wanted to talk with me about spiritual things. Well, shortly after graduation I was up in the mountains and I went to get my hair cut, and as I sat down in the shop I was holding a book that dealt with spiritual issues. The lady who was going to cut my hair was maybe 25 or 30 years old, and I remember she said to me, she goes, oh, is that a book on spiritual issues? Do you mind if I ask you some questions? And I remember thinking, yes. I just took a class on apologetics. Bring it on. I'm ready with an answer.

paragraphs.heading: Speaking the truth in love
paragraphs.edited: This lesson is not really about the biblical position on homosexuality, or solving the problem of evil. It's not really about any particular issue at all. Rather, it's about speaking the truth in love. As followers of Christ, we need to have the courage to speak truth and to speak it boldly, but not arrogantly, as I did to the lady who was cutting my hair. Do it out of compassion. Do it with a heart of graciousness and kindness toward those who need the truth to set them free.

Rather, it's about speaking the truth in love. As followers of Christ, we need to have the courage to speak truth and to speak it boldly. But not arrogantly as I did to the lady who was cutting my hair, but do it out of compassion. Do it with a heart of graciousness and kindness towards those who need the truth to set them free.

paragraphs.heading: The unmerciful servant
paragraphs.edited: In Matthew 18:21-35, Jesus tells the story of the unmerciful servant. Here is a servant who was forgiven a massive sum from the king, but then he turns around and demands that another servant, who owes him just a few dollars, pay him back. Now, why was this servant so demanding and didn't show forgiveness to the other servant? It's because he failed to truly understand and appreciate how much the king had forgiven him.

paragraphs.edited: I think sometimes we fail to really show grace and love to other people because we don't really understand the depth of sin in our own hearts, and don't understand how much God has forgiven us. If we really want to be able to love people the way God wants us to love them, it begins by first understanding how much God has loved us. If you are willing to speak truth boldly, but do it from a heart motivated by love, and if you're willing to listen to other people's stories because you care about them, and also willing to share yours, I really believe that God could use you to do powerful things within your generation.
